title: Dash and body camera video – stranded motorist assist on I-80 near Rock Springs, April 8, 2023 (meth, fentanyl pills, stolen pistols)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wyoming Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All dash camera (in-car) and body-worn camera video, with audio, recorded by Wyoming Highway Patrol troopers during a motorist assist on Interstate 80 east of Rock Springs, Sweetwater County, on the evening of April 8, 2023. A trooper stopped to help a woman from California whose car had run out of gas. A man from Iowa then came out of a nearby ditch. A drug detection dog named Becky alerted on the car, and troopers found about 11.5 pounds of suspected methamphetamine, about 3.7 pounds of marijuana, 2,186 suspected fentanyl pills and two stolen pistols. Both people were arrested. The incident was described in a Wyoming Highway Patrol news release in April 2023.

I also request the incident and arrest reports and any photographs of the seized drugs and firearms.

I ask that redacted versions be released rather than withholding records in full. Original digital video files are preferred, delivered by download link. If the criminal cases are still open and records are withheld for that reason, please tell me when they may become releasable.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Mattias Jussila

title: Detailing Arrangements for Tech Force Staff from Treasury

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Detailing Arrangements for Tech Force Staff from Treasury
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

There has been very little transparency into how OPM's Tech Force is being staffed and deployed to agencies. However, there have been two reported examples where Sam Corcos has used Tech Force staff from Treasury to perform technical work in the Technology Transfer Service at GSA (vs. using GSA staff, Tech Force or not). Looking at the LinkedIn page for people affiliated with Tech Force (, and it seems like a significant number report their agency as the Treasury (see https://www.linkedin.com/company/ustechforce/people/) and some of these Treasury hires report being forward deployed engineers, which seems to be military-related work.

It seems at first glance that Treasury is being used as a base to deploy individuals to other agencies instead of hiring them there. Unfortunately, this seems similar to how DOGE would hire staff at OPM and GSA and then detail them out to many other agencies as a way to obscure its tracks. I would hope Tech Force is not doing anything similar, and would appreciate any information that would clear up their record. 

Specifically, I am looking for the following bits of information.
1. Either individual SF-50s (can be redacted from personal details) or a table showing the hiring dates (and departure if relevant) for Tech Force Staff hired by Treasury or IRS
2. If Tech Force staff are technically OPM employees and detailed to Treasury, I would like copies of those detailing agreements and similar information about when the detail started and possibly ended.
3. I would like detailing agreements from Treasury/IRS to other agencies. Specifically, I am most interested in these details:
     a. Treasury/IRS to GSA (for Sam Corcos). I am aware of Ryan Parker and Justin Adelman being two Tech Force employees who have detailed in such a way, but this list is not necessarily exhaustive.
     b. Where-ever so-called "Forward Deployed Engineers" have been detailed to if it's outside of the IRS/Treasury
     c. Any details to DHS or one of its subsidiary agencies like ICE, especially if the detail is from the IRS
     d. Total counts of Tech Force staff in Treasury/IRS and how many of each have been detailed outside of the agency

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Harris

To Whom It May Concern:

The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is submitting this request for records under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act. related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

*Background*
Axon (also known as Axon Enterprise, Inc.) is a company that describes itself as providing “public safety technology solutions” to a variety of customers, many of which are law enforcement agencies based in the United States. For reference, Axon’s website is www.axon.com. These “solutions” may be equipment, software, or “artificial intelligence”-driven analysis of video and data. Some examples of equipment, software, and services created and sold by Axon include (but are not limited to):
• the TASER, a conducted energy device
• body-worn cameras (often referred to as “Axon Body”)
• Axon Fusus, a platform used to integrate cameras and other data into a “real-time crime center” (RTCC) 
• Axon 911, an AI-driven assistant platform for dispatchers
• Axon Evidence, a platform to integrate evidence and other information
• Axon Outpost, an automated license plate reader (ALPR) system
• Axon Lightpost, an ALPR system designed for integration with streetlights
• the Axon AI Era Plan, a collection of AI-driven analysis software (www.axon.com/products/axon-ai-era-plan)
• Axon Vision, an AI-driven video analysis system
• Axon Assistant, an AI-driven chatbot
• Axon Draft One, an AI-assisted police report generation feature
• Axon Records, a records management system
• Axon virtual reality training
• Axon Air DFR, a drone-as-first-responder platform, which may also include drones created by a company called Skydio

Axon provides services or devices to the majority of policing agencies in the United States. Axon often “bundles” services and devices into a single contract, makes adjustments and additions to existing agreements for the provision of new goods, and is designated a “sole source provider” during the procurement process. Contracts and agreements may be active for many years and may include “escalator” clauses that describe ongoing and increasing costs for the procurement over the life of the contract.

*Timeframe*
The requested records are all those related to agreements with Axon active during the year 2026, as well as those agreements related to devices, services, and payments to be provided in the future. 

*Requested records*
This public records request is for materials related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

1. CONTRACT AND AGREEMENTS
All contracts, memorandums of understanding, and any other written agreements between this agency and Axon. Response records included all associated amendments, exhibits, and supplemental and supporting documentation for each agreement, including any amendments and materials generated subsequent to the initial contract agreement. If this agency uses any Axon product, including but not limited to the ones listed above, agreements referencing those products are responsive to this request; this includes all agreements related to “trial” or “free” periods of use. 

2. FINANCIAL AND PROCUREMENT MATERIALS
All relevant procurement and financial documents and agreements, as well as records of financial transactions, exchanges, and obligations relevant to devices and services procured from Axon. Some of these details and documents may be included as part of the Master Services and Purchasing Agreement or related quotes. 
Responsive materials include: 
• quote materials
• invoices and bills
• records describing specific pricing for each associated line item, including the unit price, the quantity procured of each unit, and associated pricing components. If additional products will be procured over the life of the contract, please be sure to provide records that reflect future acquisitions under the agreement and their cost. 
• receipts
• Requests for Proposal to which Axon provided a response
• bidding materials provided by Axon
• justifications for sole source designation (or equivalent designation, if different terminology is used in your jurisdiction) and associated materials. Responsive materials include any letters and drafts provided by Axon, any supporting materials provided by the company, and any related resolutions and materials generated by the jurisdiction in the process of obtaining a sole source designation for Axon. If the company is not subject to competitive purchasing procedures for a reason that is not a “sole source designation” (for example, because the agreement is part of a cooperative or collaborative purchase), please provide records sufficient to show why the company or the contract is not subject to competitive bidding. 
• records sufficient to show the projected ongoing cost of the agreement with Axon
• records reflecting any discounts or other calculations that were figured into the costs associated with this procurement

*Provision of records*
We ask that these materials be provided on a rolling basis; please provide materials to us as your office collects and reviews records. Please contact us for further discussion regarding the search and release of these materials.

*Fees*
In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform us of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes. Please assess fees appropriately in accordance with a public records request being made in the public interest for research and journalism purposes.

*Format of responsive records*
I request that all records be disclosed in their native, digital format and transmitted to us electronically. 

*Contact information*
If you need any more information in order to process the request, or cannot process a portion of the request for any reason, please respond to the email address on this request or “beryl@eff.org”. Please let us know if a phone call will be necessary or desirable; such contact information will be provided upon request.

Thank you very much for your time and help.

Sincerely,
Beryl Lipton

title: FBI: Fingerprint submission, Portland Police Bureau case 94-99422 / Multnomah County ME case 94-2962 (Oct. 1994)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FBI: Fingerprint submission, Portland Police Bureau case 94-99422 / Multnomah County ME case 94-2962 (Oct. 1994)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Freedom of Information Act, I request the following records:

1. Any fingerprint submission received from the Portland Police Bureau, the Multnomah County Medical Examiner's Office, or the Oregon State Police between October 18, 1994 and December 31, 1994 concerning an unidentified deceased white female found in a Portland, Oregon motel on or about October 18, 1994 (PPB case no. 94-99422; Multnomah County ME case no. 94-2962).

2. Any response, search result, "non-identification" notice, or correspondence returned to the submitting agency about that submission.

3. Any later search, comparison, or retention of those prints, including in the unidentified person or unknown deceased files.

4. If no submission was received, a statement to that effect.

This request rests on the Multnomah County Medical Examiner's follow-up report, entry of 10/20/94, 09:03 hrs, which states Portland Police ID ran the prints locally and through AFIS and "will forward the prints to the FBI." I do not know whether the submission was made. The decedent has never been identified, and no named individual is the subject of this request.

For context, this case has long been discussed online: 

https://websleuths.com/threads/or-portland-whtfem-35-55-up9936-suicide-hotel-surgical-scars-lft-knee-rt-breast-dec94.165575/

https://unidentified-awareness.fandom.com/wiki/Multnomah_County_Jane_Doe_(1994)

https://www.reddit.com/r/UnresolvedMysteries/comments/8znefv/in_1994_a_woman_was_found_dead_after_having/

Thank you for the work that the bureau does each and every day, and thank you for the commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

Nicholas Lee

Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of all shifts worked by all Boston Police Department employees from 1/1/2025 to 12/31/2025. Please include the following fields of information:

City of Boston Employee ID (6 digit ID)

Employee last name
Employee middle name or initial
Assigned description 
Charged description
Start time
End time
Worked hours
Billed hours


I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at adasuss@bu.edu.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. 3. Staff Identifiers: The full name, official job title/position, CPS-issued email address, and CPS system User ID of the CPS employee(s) who created, edited, modified, or accessed the records described in Item #1. 

PREEMPTIVE CLARIFICATIONS AND WAIVERS (PLEASE READ CAREFULLY):
• NO STUDENT PRIVACY ISSUES: I am NOT requesting any student names, student ID numbers, initials, or any other Personally Identifiable Information (PII) regarding any student. You are fully authorized and expected to redact all student information. I am strictly requesting the underlying narrative of the events (with student names redacted as "Student A", etc.), the rule violated, the disciplinary action taken, and the adult staff members involved.

• NO PERSONAL EMPLOYEE PRIVACY ISSUES: I am waiving any request for personal employee information, including home addresses, personal cell phone numbers, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, or personal (non-CPS) email addresses.

Under Illinois FOIA precedent, public employees acting in their official capacity (using government systems and credentials) do not have a protectable privacy interest in their official actions. • Redaction over Withholding: If any portion of a responsive record is deemed exempt, you are required to redact only that specific portion and release the remainder of the document. You may not withhold an entire document because a name is present.
• Data Dictionary: If you claim that the systems used to store these records (e.g., ASPEN, ICT) do not possess an audit trail or modification history, please provide the "Data Dictionary" or System Administrator Manual for the software that proves the system does not track this information.
• Fallback for Staff Names: If you determine that the actual name of an employee must be redacted, you are still required to provide their official job title/position, their CPS email address, their User ID, and the date/time of their action. The public has a right to know the role of the official altering public records.

For William Claude Reavis Math and Science Specialty School (834 E. 50th St, Chicago, IL) for the period of March 1, 2022 through August 31, 2022, I am requesting:

Incident and Disciplinary Records: Copies of all Incident Reports, Student Code of Conduct (SCC) Referrals, Disciplinary Notices, and Misconduct Reports generated at the school level during the requested timeframe. (Please note: Do not deny this request on the basis that a specific "Safety and Security Department" database does not exist. 2. Audit Trails and Metadata: Any existing audit trails, system metadata, modification histories, or access logs for the records described in Item #1. This includes the date and time the record was created or modified. 

3. Staff Identifiers: The full name, official job title/position, CPS-issued email address, and CPS system User ID of the CPS employee(s) who created, edited, modified, or accessed the records described in Item #1. 

PREEMPTIVE CLARIFICATIONS AND WAIVERS (PLEASE READ CAREFULLY): 
• NO STUDENT PRIVACY ISSUES: I am NOT requesting any student names, student ID numbers, initials, or any other Personally Identifiable Information (PII) regarding any student. You are fully authorized and expected to redact all student information. I am strictly requesting the underlying narrative of the events (with student names redacted as "Student A", etc.), the rule violated, the disciplinary action taken, and the adult staff members involved. 

• NO PERSONAL EMPLOYEE PRIVACY ISSUES: I am waiving any request for personal employee information, including home addresses, personal cell phone numbers, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, or personal (non-CPS) email addresses.

Under Illinois FOIA precedent, public employees acting in their official capacity (using government systems and credentials) do not have a protectable privacy interest in their official actions. communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Unlike many other websites operated by the federal government, America.gov does not participate in the Digital Analytics Program (DAP), which is also administered by the GSA. This means that it does not contribute any data on its website traffic to https://analytics.usa.gov/, which undermines trust in claims about its popularity or effectiveness for the American public.

I would like to request the following documentation for FOIA purposes:
1. Any communications related to why America.gov does not include any analytics capability provided by DAP.
2. Any internal measurements of America.gov traffic that have been tracked by GSA. These might include both web analytics or it might also include data about chats initiated every week to the Large Language Models (LLMs) that power AI chats on the site (I believe it might be xAI Grok and/or Google Gemini)

I would expect this information would be provided as briefing materials to senior staff via email and could be found by searching for words like "traffic" or "analytics", etc. and "America.gov" I would expect these emails and communications to be from early-mid 2026 or later.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.
